solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Entertaining at first, Boris past sell-by date? Sure!

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the name that follows
to entertain a guest is to hold them inside your home, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: food past its sell-by date has gone stale
the opening letter of Boris

explanation.surface: A jibe that Boris Johnson is a politician well past his sell-by date, delivered with sarcastic agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The word for past its sell-by date holds the first letter of Boris in its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something stable is steady and secure, so the adjective works as a synonym for sure in the sense of firmly fixed.

clue.text: (& 25dn.) Seat - the source of many a politician's speech?

definitions.text: the source of many a politician's speech

blocks.note: first meaning: the seat or bottom, the part of the body you sit on, in its crude anatomical form

blocks.clueFragment: the source of many a politician's speech
blocks.note: second meaning: politicians are said to talk out of their backsides, so that is where the speech comes from

explanation.surface: A sneer at politicians, whose speeches seem to come from the seat of their trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Typical Private Eye vulgarity: 'talking out of your arse' is British slang for speaking nonsense, so the crude anatomical word fits both halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Seat is a polite word for the buttocks and backside, and the answer is the vulgar British word for the opening there.

clue.text: Sex with celebrity's butt in travel broadcast is standard viewing these days

indicators.note: a butt is the tail end of something, so only the last letter is wanted
to broadcast is to scatter widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order
in places the preceding pieces inside the scrambled word

blocks.note: it is a coy old word for sex
the final letter of celebrity
taken as written, ready to be shuffled

explanation.surface: A grumble that television now serves up sex and celebrity bottoms in place of decent travel shows.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcast looks like part of the TV picture, but it is the signal to rearrange the word before it; the two-letter piece for sex is a coy old euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: Unscripted shows about ordinary people and celebrities fill the schedules now, making them the typical fare people watch.

clue.text: Sun associated with former leader of Conservatives in casual wear – downfall of many a politician

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so only the first letter is wanted
in puts the preceding letter inside the item of clothing

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for Sunday or sun
ex- means former
an open summer shoe is casual footwear
the first letter of Conservatives

explanation.surface: A tabloid paper linked with an ex-Tory leader caught out in his weekend clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Sun looks like the tabloid newspaper, but it just gives S. C sits inside the open shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Many politicians have resigned after affairs were exposed in the press, so a scandal of that kind is a classic career-ender.

clue.text: Sexual moves banks are not so keen on now?

definitions.text: banks are not so keen on now

blocks.note: first meaning: passes or approaches made at someone you fancy

blocks.clueFragment: banks are not so keen on now
blocks.note: second meaning: loans of money, which lenders became wary of after the credit crunch

explanation.walkthrough: One word covers both unwanted passes and money lent up front, which banks tightened up on after 2008.
explanation.definitionFit: Romantic overtures and sums lent beforehand are both standard senses of the plural noun.

clue.text: Agog audience taking in Barack finally exposed

indicators.note: finally asks for only the closing letter of the name before it
to take something in is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: people agog gape at the scene: they are starers
the last letter of Barack

explanation.surface: An astonished crowd catches sight of President Obama with his clothes off.
explanation.walkthrough: Starkers is British slang for stark naked.
explanation.definitionFit: To be starkers is to be completely naked, which is exposed in the bodily sense.

clue.text: Bush's guts upset by "faggot" embracing Republicans' leader – "sickly"

indicators.note: guts are the insides, so only the middle letters are wanted
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way
the leader goes first, so only the opening letter is wanted
to embrace is to hold in the arms, so one word wraps around another

blocks.note: the two inner letters of Bush
an offensive slang term for a homosexual man
the first letter of Republicans

explanation.surface: A slur on President Bush, made queasy by an insult hurled while he hugs a party grandee.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of Bush turned over, then the slang word holding the Republicans' initial.
explanation.definitionFit: Sickly and sugary both describe something cloying and excessively sweet, as in sentimental writing.

clue.text: Top royal squeezes butt into skimpy underwear

indicators.note: something that squeezes another thing presses tightly around it, holding it inside

blocks.note: a brassiere, a scanty undergarment
a butt is the end of something, such as a cigarette

explanation.surface: A senior royal forcing her bottom into undersized knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's long-running nickname for Queen Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: In Private Eye the late Queen, the most senior member of the royal family, was always called Brenda.

clue.text: (& 22dn.) A thing of the past according to Brown? Roar "Tits!"

definitions.text: A thing of the past according to Brown

blocks.note: a boom is a deep roaring sound
slang for breasts, collectively the bust

explanation.surface: Gordon Brown boasting that something is over, while someone bellows a rude word.
explanation.walkthrough: The grid takes the phrase without its AND. Gordon Brown, as Chancellor, repeatedly claimed to have ended boom and bust.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown's famous promise was that the economic cycle of rapid growth followed by collapse had been abolished, making it history in his telling.

clue.text: "Go down" gradually, with mechanical assistance?

blocks.note: surface reading: a sex act performed slowly with the help of a device
setter's reading: descending a cliff face slowly on a rope with a friction device

explanation.walkthrough: The quote marks around go down point to the slang sense; the plain sense is a climber lowering themselves down a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers lower themselves down rock faces using a fixed rope and a braking device, which is a controlled descent aided by equipment.

clue.text: Apt term for fat cat's untaxed earnings?

definitions.text: Apt term for fat cat's untaxed earnings?

blocks.clueFragment: Apt term for fat cat's untaxed earnings?
blocks.note: surface reading: a fitting word for an executive's obscene salary

blocks.clueFragment: Apt term for fat cat's untaxed earnings?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the accounting term for earnings before deductions, which also sounds disgusting

explanation.walkthrough: A fat cat is an overpaid boss. The accounting phrase for pay before tax contains a word that also means revolting, hence apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings before tax and other deductions are called by this accounting phrase, and for a fat cat the amount is also obscene.

clue.text: (& 15ac.) Clinton "erect, say, for fooling around" is in poor taste

indicators.note: fooling around means messing about, so these letters are played with and reordered
poor means badly made, so the following word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: three words taken as written to be shuffled
taken as written, also to be shuffled

explanation.surface: Bill Clinton's sexual antics with an intern recalled as a joke in bad taste.
explanation.walkthrough: Clinton suggests Bill and the Lewinsky affair, but the definition is Hillary Clinton, who held the US foreign-affairs post.
explanation.definitionFit: Hillary Clinton served as the US cabinet officer in charge of foreign affairs under Obama, so her surname stands for the job.

clue.text: Taking Thatcher's lead, into character assassination, he's out to get rid of pests

definitions.text: he's out to get rid of pests

indicators.note: the lead is the front position, so only the first letter is wanted
an assassination destroys its target, so the word is wrecked and its letters rebuilt

blocks.note: the first letter of Thatcher
taken as written, ready to be shuffled

explanation.surface: A politician follows Mrs Thatcher's example of attacking opponents' reputations, out to remove the vermin.
explanation.walkthrough: Character assassination reads as a phrase, but assassination is the signal working on character, with Thatcher's T added.
explanation.definitionFit: A person employed to catch and kill vermin such as rodents is a classic pest controller.

clue.text: It helps you dry off not fully frontal chicks

indicators.note: not fully means only part of the following words is used, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A towel scene in which young women are only partly nude.
explanation.walkthrough: Full frontal means nudity seen from the front; here the letters sit across the end of one word and start of the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Talcum powder is dusted on the skin after a bath to absorb moisture and keep it dry.

clue.text: So, ideal location for a new retail park, Brent, e.g. relocated round east end of Ewell?

definitions.text: So, ideal location for a new retail park

indicators.note: relocated means moved elsewhere, so the letters are moved into a new order
end of asks for only the closing letter of the town named
round means placed around, so the rearranged letters go outside the rest

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be shuffled
E is the abbreviation for east
the final letter of Ewell

explanation.surface: A sarcastic planning proposal to move a London borough's shops out to a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is ironic: the protected countryside ring is exactly where developers are not supposed to build. Brent is a London borough and Ewell a Surrey town.
explanation.definitionFit: Protected undeveloped land around a city is what developers covet for out-of-town shopping, so calling it ideal is sarcasm.

clue.text: see 11ac.
Error-prone old politician, caught by slump, takes drug

indicators.note: caught by something means held inside it, so the politician sits within the other word

blocks.note: a slump is a fall in value
Lib is short for a Liberal, a party now merged into the Liberal Democrats
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A blundering former MP, laid low by a downturn, turns to drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fallible is liable to make mistakes, the same idea as being prone to error.

clue.text: Penis tip, fairly rough, not broad

indicators.note: the tip is the very end, here the first letter

blocks.note: the first letter of Penis
rude means rough or crude, and -ish means fairly so

explanation.surface: An earthy remark about anatomy, half crude and half coy.
explanation.walkthrough: Broad here means coarse or risqué, as in broad humour.
explanation.definitionFit: A prudish person avoids anything risqué, so they are the opposite of broad in the sense of coarse or bawdy.

clue.text: Fanny's weightlifting technique?

blocks.note: first meaning: in British slang fanny means the female genitals, and this is a cruder word for them
second meaning: an Olympic lift taking the bar from floor to overhead in one movement

explanation.walkthrough: Fanny's looks like a woman's name. In British English it is vulgar slang for the vulva, not the backside as in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are established senses: a vulgar slang word for female genitals, and one of the two Olympic lifts.

clue.text: Unauthorised release taken by peer

blocks.note: first meaning: secret information let out without permission
second meaning: a peer here is one who pees, and one takes a slang urination

explanation.walkthrough: Peer looks like a member of the House of Lords; read it as someone who pees.
explanation.definitionFit: A disclosure of secrets is a standard sense, and 'take a' plus the same word is slang for urinating.

clue.text: Wife's abandoned seasonal frilly material? Mingle!

indicators.note: something abandoned is left behind, so that letter is dropped

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
the season used as an adjective, as in winter coat
an openwork fabric used for frills

explanation.surface: A wife walks out on her frilly holiday lingerie, and someone urges a party guest to circulate.
explanation.definitionFit: To interlace is to weave threads together, so things become intermixed, which is a sense of mingle.

clue.text: Nameless old PM's bit of S and M?

indicators.note: nameless means without a name, so the letter standing for name is removed

blocks.note: George Canning was a British prime minister in 1827
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Gossip that an unnamed former prime minister enjoyed a little sadomasochism.
explanation.walkthrough: Take one N out of the old PM's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Beating with a cane is a common feature of sadomasochistic play, so it is one element of S and M.

clue.text: see 8dn.
"Virgin's leader is very rude contemptible person, without love" – aristocrat

indicators.note: the leader is the one in front, so only the first letter is wanted
without in its old sense means outside, so the insult sits outside the letter for love

blocks.note: the first letter of Virgin
taken as written
the most offensive British term of abuse for a despised person
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A quote calling Richard Branson, Virgin's boss, a heartless swine, framed as fit for a peer.
explanation.walkthrough: Without means outside here, not lacking: the insult wraps around O.
explanation.definitionFit: A viscount is a British nobleman ranking between an earl and a baron, so he is a member of the aristocracy.

clue.text: Supporting an arse

blocks.note: first meaning: backing someone
second meaning: the buttocks, the part at the back

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like propping up a fool; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To be firmly behind someone is to back them, and the noun is a familiar euphemism for the backside.

clue.text: see 2dn.
Famous royal keen to grab Brenda's top

indicators.note: in a top position means first, so only the opening letter is wanted
to grab is to seize and hold, so one word closes around the letter

blocks.note: keen and sharp-witted, wide awake
the opening letter of Brenda

explanation.surface: A well-known royal eager to snatch the Queen's crown or, in Eye style, her bra.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's name for the Queen, but here just gives its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert, Queen Victoria's consort, is one of the best-known members of the British royal family.

definitions.text: You might need to resort to this

indicators.note: a dysfunction means something is not working properly, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
the parenthesis says use the short form, L as on clothing sizes
taken as written, ready to be shuffled

explanation.walkthrough: Short looks like a joke about size, but it tells you to abbreviate large.
